title: K-Sample Anderson-Darling Tests
journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association

sections: 2 The k-Sample Anderson-Darling Test: Continuous Populations
3 The Finite Sample Distribution Under H0
4 Asymptotic Distribution Under H0 and Critical Points
verified_claims: the continuous k-sample statistic is a rank statistic built from a pooled empirical-distribution path
the computational formula weights squared sample-versus-pooled count differences by j times N-minus-j and therefore emphasizes pooled tails
the finite continuous null distribution can in principle be obtained by traversing all rank permutations
permutation match-or-exceed frequency is a supported way to evaluate the observed statistic
the method is nonparametric and compares sample distributions without specifying their common distribution

claim_boundary: The paper supplies the continuous no-tie statistic, tail weighting, and rank-permutation rationale only. It does not test gold, silver, monthly ratio changes, the locked half-tail activity boundary, contrarian trading, CFDs, or any performance result.
